title: Developer Onboarding — Sample Apps, Observability Hooks & Cost Budgets
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook provides a compact, opinionated onboarding path for engineers building sample applications against Redwood SDKs. The goal is to help new integrators (internal teams and pilot customers) ship a reproducible sample app with production-grade observability and a pre-configured cost budget. The document focuses on three deliverables: 1) a minimal sample app template, 2) observable telemetry hooks and golden-trace baselines, and 3) a cost-budget policy and enforcement checklist.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SDK integrators, solutions engineers, and internal onboarding mentors.
- Scope: JavaScript/TypeScript and Python sample apps that call Redwood endpoints (generation, embeddings). Not exhaustive library reference; links at the end provide SDK docs.

Why this matters:
- Sample apps are often the first contact point for teams making architectural choices. Providing consistent telemetry and cost controls prevents misconfigured experiments from becoming recurring support burdens.

Quick summary (one-minute runbook):
1) Clone the sample-app repo template and pick the runtime (node or python).
2) Wire the SDK auth and set REDWOOD_ENV=test to enable sampling policies.
3) Swap in the pre-built telemetry wrapper and enable cost-budget labels.
4) Run smoke tests and verify golden-trace against CI baseline.

Deliverable 1 — Minimal sample-app template

What you get in the template:
- 2 endpoints: /api/generate and /api/embeddings (HTTP POST).
- Built-in retries with backoff, idempotency token header, and a telemetry wrapper that emits span + token-level cost metadata.
- Environment-based routing: hosted (default), dedicated, or private-config via REDWOOD_DEPLOYMENT_MODE.

Repository layout (high level):
- src/handler.(js|py) — HTTP handler glue code.
- src/redwood_client.(js|py) — small wrapper around official SDK with telemetry hooks.
- tests/smoke — smoke tests that run against a sandbox key.
- ci/golden-trace — baseline traces and tokens used by CI gating.

Code snippets: SDK wrapper (Node)
```js
// src/redwood_client.js — minimal wrapper with telemetry hooks
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

async function generate(req) {
  const traceCtx = startTrace('sample.generate');
  const response = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: req.body.prompt });
  annotateTrace(traceCtx, { tokens: response.token_count, cost_usd: response.estimated_cost });
  endTrace(traceCtx);
  return response;
}

module.exports = { generate };
```

Deliverable 2 — Observability hooks and golden-trace baselines

Objectives:
- Provide a consistent trace/metric schema for sample apps so that support staff can triage regressions quickly.
- Create a golden trace artifact per sample app and runtime; CI must compare new traces to golden baselines and fail on large divergence.

Required telemetry fields (span attributes / metric tags):
- service.name (string) — e.g., sample-miniapp-js
- sdk.version (string) — SDK version used by the sample
- request.id (string) — unique id per external request
- model.name (string) — model variant invoked
- tokens.input, tokens.output (ints) — token counts
- cost.estimated_usd (float string) — estimated token cost for the call
- fallback.reason (optional string) — when a fallback model or route was used

Golden-trace generation workflow:
1) Run ci/golden-trace/generate.sh with a fixed seed and sandbox API key (see CI variables).
2) The script stores: a trace.json (OpenTelemetry-style), an aggregated metrics CSV, and a small replay input file.
3) CI stage 'golden-compare' executes sample app smoke tests and compares current trace.json metrics (quantiles for latency, tokens, and cost) to stored baseline thresholds.
4) If divergence > tolerance (default 15% for tokens/cost, 10% for p95 latency) the gate fails and creates a regression ticket.

Example golden-compare command (CI):
```bash
ci/golden-trace/compare.sh --baseline ci/golden-trace/sample-miniapp-js/trace.json --current tmp/trace.json --tolerance "tokens:0.15,cost:0.15,latency_p95:0.10"
```

Telemetry sampling and cost-aware retention:
- Default: sample 100% of failed requests, 10% of successful requests, and 100% of requests that exceed cost thresholds (see cost budgets).
- Use probabilistic sampling keyed by customer_id to keep longitudinal traces.

Deliverable 3 — Cost budgets and enforcement checklist

Why cost budgets: early experiments with unbounded prompts or high-temperature settings generate outsized per-token bills. We proactively apply budgets to sample apps to avoid surprises for pilot customers.

Policy (enforced by CI + runtime guards):
- Per-repo budget label: redwood.budget.monthly_usd (example default: "50").
- Runtime guard: block requests when estimated_cost > runtime_max_per_request_usd (default: 0.50).
- CI check: the sample-app must include an infra/config file with budget label and cover tests that verify guard behavior.

Config matrix (example):
| field | type | default | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| redwood.budget.monthly_usd | number | 50 | monthly budget to show in onboarding UI |
| runtime_max_per_request_usd | number | 0.5 | requests estimating higher are rejected with 429 |
| telemetry.sample_success_pct | number | 10 | percent of successful traces to record |
| telemetry.sample_failure_pct | number | 100 | record all failures |
| deployment_mode | enum | hosted | hosted | dedicated | private |

Runtime guard behavior (pseudo-step):
1) Before request execution compute estimated_cost_usd = model_price_per_token * (tokens.input + expected_output_tokens).
2) If estimated_cost_usd > runtime_max_per_request_usd then return 429 with payload: { "error": "request_exceeds_budget", "estimated_cost": "0.73" } and emit telemetry event cost.rejected.
3) If telemetry.sampled then record full trace. Always increment cost counters for billing estimation.

Alerting and dashboarding recommendations:
- Dashboard: Sample App Observability — per-sample p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, cost per request, rejected-by-budget count.
- Alerts (recommended):
  - high-cost-runway: when 7-day rolling spend / monthly_budget > 0.6 → PagerDuty (P2)
  - budget-rejection-surge: when budget rejection rate > 1% over 30m → Slack channel notify + ticket (P3)
  - regressive-golden-trace: when CI golden-compare fails → create regression ticket and tag engineering oncall (P1 if production customers rely on the sample).

Procedures for sample app maintainers (step-by-step)
1) Fork the template and set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_DEPLOYMENT_MODE in repo secrets.
2) Edit config/budget.yml and pick redwood.budget.monthly_usd.
3) Add smoke tests in tests/smoke that exercise: cheap generation, expensive generation (to test guard), and embeddings.
4) Generate golden traces via ci/golden-trace/generate.sh and commit artifacts to ci/golden-trace/.
5) Submit a PR with description of changed telem fields and cost settings. Assign reviewers from the SDK team.
6) After merge, run the onboarding checklist and confirm the app appears in the internal sample-app catalog (managed by devx oncall).

Troubleshooting common issues
- Symptom: CI golden-compare fails due to tokens mismatch.
  - Likely causes: SDK model version bump, underlying tokenizer change, or prompt change.
  - Action: run local trace with identical seed, capture token counts, and open a regression ticket with the trace artifact attached.
- Symptom: Unexpected 429 from runtime guard in smoke tests.
  - Likely causes: misconfigured runtime_max_per_request_usd, or model price per token changed.
  - Action: Verify config/budget.yml and look up model price in product catalog; update budget or pick smaller model.
- Symptom: No traces show up in CI.
  - Likely causes: missing telemetry env var, sample disabled in CI sampling policy, or instrumentation mismatch.
  - Action: verify TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true in CI, ensure SDK wrapper emits required attributes, and run trace locally to validate format.

Operational ownership and handoff
- Initial owner: the authoring team (author listed in this doc).
- Long-term ownership: devx-samples rotation — a two-week oncall that triages sample-app regressions. Add the repo to the devx-samples roster by filing an onboarding ticket with #devx-oncall.
- Who to page on regression: @sdk-oncall for SDK issues; @platform-oncall for infra/CI issues.

Security and privacy notes
- Never commit REDWOOD_API_KEY or customer data into the sample repo. Use CI secrets and scrubbed replay inputs only.
- Golden traces must exclude PII; use synthetic inputs or anonymized copies.

Appendices
A) Example telemetry event (OpenTelemetry-like JSON):
```json
{
  "resource": {"service.name":"sample-miniapp-js","sdk.version":"1.4.1"},
  "spans": [
    {"name":"redwood.generate","attributes":{"request.id":"r-123","model.name":"redwood-small","tokens.input":54,"tokens.output":78,"cost.estimated_usd":"0.06"},"status":"OK"}
  ]
}
```

B) Example CI golden-compare summary output (when passing):
```
SUMMARY: tokens.avg delta 3.2% | cost.avg delta 1.1% | latency_p95 delta 4.8% | RESULT PASS
```

C) Useful links and references:
- SDK docs: https://internal.redwood.dev/sdk (public-facing SDK docs are canonical).
- CI golden trace runner: ci/golden-trace/README.md in the template repo.
- Oncall roster and sample-app catalog: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support-top-issues/devx-oncall-roster (internal page).

summary: A concise onboarding playbook for sample apps with telemetry and cost controls.
